skeptics: VERDICT: confirmed. _attrs_print (added by this PR) reads every property by reflection; only UserStringCount is skipped, so LayerIndex is fingerprinted (the test fixture even lists it). BoxSession.commit calls remove_layer_if_empty(HOLDING_LAYER) -> doc.Layers.Delete (gordium_rhino.py:1393); cancel/rollback and recover_held delete layers too. The holding layer is made before the Gordium::Context::* layers. Deleted layers are not written to the .3dm and the table is renumbered on reopen (from knowledge, not run), so every outline's LayerIndex drops; is_edited -> True, kept_on_clear -> True, _clear_context strips CONTEXT_KEY and sets EDITED_KEY: the whole old neighbourhood stays forever. The new-Rhino-property point holds at lower weight.

VERDICT: confirmed. GEOM_KEY is saved in the file (gordium_rhino.py:2606-2609) and compared on every later _clear_context, including the second-address clear in sync_context. Gordium deletes layers itself (remove_layer_if_empty; cancel; recover_held). A deleted layer keeps its slot for the session; layers made later sit at higher indices; renumbered on read. The consequence follows from _clear_context 2485-2490, then _edited_pieces / skip_edited stop those pieces being drawn fresh. A new readable ObjectAttributes property in a later Rhino has the same effect. Fix: layer by Id/FullPath, material/linetype by Id. (Rhino not run.)
